title: A bird survey-temperature slope change above 15 C was clear only in the later western US sample in 1990-2024
abstract: We tested whether the slope of recorded bird taxa against survey start temperature changes above 15 C. We reused 9,876 accepted surveys in four US states and made 7,068 consecutive-year pairs with the same route and observer. Separate models for two regions and two periods controlled for survey timing, effort, weather, and state-year changes. All four fitted slope changes were negative. Only the 2007-2024 western change excluded zero after correction for four tests: -1.93 taxa per 5 C, with an interval from -3.31 to -0.56. Its fitted cool and warm slopes were +0.76 and -1.17 taxa per 5 C. The change remained clear with end-temperature control but became uncertain with close-date and fair-weather restrictions. This result supports a test of curved observation models. It does not establish a common biological threshold. Selected accepted runs, sparse warm western records, model choices, and unknown detection rates limit inference. We did not test pollution or extreme heat effects.

display.caption: Warm minus cool temperature slopes at a 15 C model knot. Intervals use route clusters and a correction for four tests. Only the later West interval excludes zero.
